summary:
I checked the statistics against statistics_v3.json and statistics_confirmatory.json. Every headline inferential number in the manuscript matches the result files, so the core inference is sound. Specifically:
- Holm adjustments recomputed by hand: H1 families of 7, H3 primary family of 4, decomposition family of 3, hull family of 2, extreme-coverage family of 16.
- Sign tests, Hodges-Lehmann (HL) ratios and geometric-mean bootstrap CIs match.
- TOST p-values (margin 0.01 on CTR23, 0.02 on held-out data) match.
- The C-H2 binomial critical value (3 for Binomial(17, 0.05)) and the C-H3 decision rule are implemented as written.
- The unit of analysis is the dataset, and one-sided tests are used only for H1, as stated.
- Since the plan commit ccba99b, analyze_confirmatory.py is unchanged. Only cosmetic changes were made to tests.py (NaN handling) and refit_scales.py (task listing).

The remaining problems concern reporting completeness and claim accuracy rather than arithmetic, but a hostile referee will find several of them:
1. The confirmatory study is called "pre-registered" under a standard the paper itself rejects in Section 5.7. The repository is described both as "public" and as to be made public "upon acceptance".
2. Pre-registered secondary analyses that are unfavourable to SDLC are not reported. On held-out data, SDLC-hull is larger than S-NCP-hull (geometric-mean ratio 1.04, 10/7 datasets).
3. Worst-slab coverage (WSC) is promised in Section 5.5 and was requested in cycle 1, but is never reported. SDLC is lower than S-NCP on 20/27 datasets (p = 0.0003).
4. The scale-decile evidence shown is the non-significant summary, while the strong, two-sided reallocation pattern is not shown.
5. One sentence about the ESS >= 50 shift subset is false.
6. Highlights 2 and 4 overstate the results.
7. Where the bootstrap CI of the geometric mean includes 1, the "smaller" claims against S-NCP rest on a skewed signed-rank test, without the promised sign-test column.

All fixes can be done from existing result files in a few hours; no new experiment is needed.

issues.title: "Pre-registered" label for the confirmatory replication cannot be verified and contradicts the paper's own standard and its data statement
issues.evidence:
The paper applies two standards to the same kind of evidence.
- For CTR23, Section 5.7 (manuscript_filled.md line ~240) says the configuration was committed to version control but "These expectations were not registered with a third party, and we do not call the study pre-registered."
- The confirmatory plan is equally a git commit (ccba99b, 2026-11-18 09:49:14, branch claude/amazing-maxwell-i1mihd), with no third-party registry. Yet the label "pre-registered" appears in the abstract, Highlight 4 (implicitly), Section 6.5, the Table 7 caption, Section 7.1, the Conclusion, Supplementary S6 and the cover letter.

The repository's public status is also stated inconsistently:
- Supplementary S6 (line 506) and PREREGISTRATION_confirmatory.md say the plan was "committed to the public repository".
- The Data and code availability statement (line ~530) says code "will be deposited in a public repository [repository URL] upon acceptance".
- The cover letter says the plan "was made public before evaluation".

Git author timestamps are set by the committer and cannot be verified by a referee. The cycle-1 corrective action (C1-01 item 1) was to keep "pre-registered" only with a verifiable public snapshot; that fix is therefore inadequate for the confirmatory study. The timeline is otherwise plausible: confirmatory raw_eval_v3 first appears in commit c3cad49 at 10:10, after ccba99b.
issues.corrective_action:
1. Pick one of two wordings and use it everywhere.
   (a) If the plan was in fact on a public, third-party-timestamped host before evaluation (a public GitHub push, Software Heritage or Zenodo record), cite that URL or DOI and the timestamp in Section 5.7 and S6.
   (b) Otherwise, replace "pre-registered" with "analysis plan fixed in advance (version-controlled commit ccba99b, timestamp 2026-11-18 09:49 UTC, before any confirmatory evaluation; not registered with a third party)". Apply this in the abstract, Section 6.5 and its heading text, the Table 7 caption, Section 7.1, the Conclusion, S6 and the cover letter. This is the same standard Section 5.7 applies to CTR23.
2. Remove "public" from S6 and PREREGISTRATION_confirmatory.md unless (a) holds.
3. Make the cover letter consistent with the data statement.
4. Disclose in S6 that tests.py (NaN-safe holm/paired_summary) and refit_scales.py (task enumeration) changed after the plan commit, and say why this does not affect the results. Also state why the equivalence margin is 0.02 here but 0.01 in Section 6.3.

issues.title: Pre-registered secondary analyses are omitted from the manuscript, including an unfavourable hull result and the S10 comparisons, and the script deviates from the plan
issues.evidence:
PREREGISTRATION_confirmatory.md Section 4 lists these secondary analyses: price vs DLS; upper-tail, top-5% and top-1% coverage; empty-set rate; worst sigma-decile coverage; "the C-H3 comparisons under decile strata (S10)"; and "hull variants". Section 5 promises they will be reported "whatever their direction". Section 6.5 reports only top-1% coverage, worst sigma-decile coverage and the price.

Omitted:
- **Hull variants.** results/confirmatory/statistics_confirmatory.json summary gives size_geo 1.363 for SDLC-hull and 1.311 for S-NCP-hull. I seed-averaged the S5, alpha = 0.1 runs in results/confirmatory/raw_eval_v3 (without the modal-K filter). SDLC-hull / S-NCP-hull has a geometric-mean ratio of 1.040, is smaller on only 10/17 datasets, and the two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.71. SDLC-hull / BCCP-hull: 0.893, 13/4, p = 0.007.
- **S10 comparisons.** statistics_confirmatory.json 'C-H3_S10_descriptive' exists (SDLC/S-NCP 0.988, 14/3) but is not reported anywhere.
- **Deviation from the plan.** analyze_confirmatory.py computes S10 comparisons only for ("S-Res", "S-NCP", "S-CQR") and omits S-HPD, although the plan says "the C-H3 comparisons", meaning all four comparators.
- **Empty-set rate** (SDLC 0.0003 vs S-NCP 0.0) is not reported.
- **No per-dataset table.** No per-dataset confirmatory size table is in the supplement, although tables/C3_per_dataset_size.csv exists.

Section 7.2 item 4 still says SDLC-hull "loses part of the advantage". On held-out data it has none against S-NCP-hull, and on CTR23 its geometric-mean ratio is 1.014.

issues.title: Worst-slab coverage is promised in Section 5.5 and requested in cycle 1, but never reported; it is clearly unfavourable to SDLC
issues.evidence:
Section 5.5 (line 227) lists "worst-slab coverage (WSC) [@cauchois2021knowing]" as a metric. Cycle-1 C1-04 item 3 asked for Holm-tested WSC differences among stratified methods. The response to C1-04 reports sigma-decile coverage and empty sets but is silent on WSC. WSC appears only as an unlabelled column in Supplementary Table S9 (variants only); it is absent from Table 2 and from the main text.

From results/per_dataset_main_v3.csv (column wsc, 27 datasets with a value):

| Comparison | Mean WSC | SDLC lower on | Two-sided Wilcoxon p (unadjusted) | Sign-test p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SDLC vs S-NCP | 0.848 vs 0.887 | 20/27 | 0.0003 | 0.019 |
| SDLC vs S-HPD | 0.848 vs 0.884 | 22/27 | 0.001 | 0.0015 |

SDLC is higher than BCCP (21/27, p = 0.010). Leaving out a promised metric that goes against the proposed method is selective reporting that a referee will catch.
issues.corrective_action:
1. Add a WSC column (and wsc_n) to Table 2.
2. Add the four SDLC-vs-stratified WSC comparisons to the Holm family "Extreme coverage vs stratified" in analyze3.py, so the family has 20 tests, and report them in Section 6.3 "What the gain costs" in one sentence with the Holm p-values.
3. Mention WSC in the abstract's trade-off clause ("lower coverage of the noisiest inputs and of the worst covariate slab").
4. Report WSC on the held-out data as a descriptive addition. My unfiltered computation gives 0.859 vs 0.873 for S-NCP, 8/17 higher, so the CTR23 result does not clearly replicate. Say so.

issues.title: Sigma-decile evidence: the statistic reported is not significant, while the decisive two-sided reallocation pattern goes unreported
issues.evidence:
Section 6.3 and Fig. 4 give "The worst coverage over deciles of sigma-hat(x) was 0.769 for SDLC against 0.793 for S-NCP", and the abstract says gains "came with lower coverage of the noisiest inputs". Per dataset (results/per_dataset_main_v3.csv, sig_worst), SDLC is lower on only 17 of 31 datasets (two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.49), so the reported statistic gives no evidence of a difference.

The actual pattern, from seed-averaged sig_cov_9 / sig_cov_0 in raw_eval_v3 (alpha = 0.1, S5, full calibration):

| sigma-hat decile | SDLC | S-NCP | SDLC lower on | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Top (noisiest) | 0.818 | 0.936 | 31/31 | < 1e-6 |
| Bottom (quietest) | 0.900 | 0.836 | 0/31 (higher on 31/31) | < 1e-6 |

Held-out data, top decile: 0.832 vs 0.932, lower on 17/17.

This is exactly the reallocation that the Section 4.3 remark predicts, and it is far larger than the worst-decile difference shown. S-NCP under-covers the quietest inputs to the same extent that SDLC under-covers the noisiest. The current text overstates SDLC's cost on the worst-decile metric and understates it on the top decile.
issues.corrective_action:
1. In Section 6.3 and Fig. 4, report coverage in the top and bottom sigma-hat deciles for SDLC, S-NCP, S-HPD and BCCP, with dataset-level Wilcoxon and sign tests (add them to the Holm family of issue 3). Keep the worst-decile figure but state that it does not differ significantly (17/31, p = 0.49).
2. Rephrase the abstract and Section 7.1 as "coverage is shifted from the noisiest to the quietest inputs (top sigma-decile coverage 0.82 vs 0.94 for S-NCP; bottom 0.90 vs 0.84)".
3. Add the held-out values from statistics_confirmatory.json and raw_eval_v3.

issues.title: False sentence: restricting the tilt analysis to the ESS >= 50 datasets does change the ordering
issues.corrective_action:
1. Replace the sentence with an accurate one, for example: "On the 15 datasets with ESS >= 50, S-NCP, S-HPD and SDLC remained above every marginal method, but BCCP (0.754) and S-CQR (0.761) fell slightly below DCP (0.765)."
2. Add dataset-level 95% CIs (bootstrap over datasets) for the gamma = 2 upper-stratum coverage, or Wilcoxon tests of SDLC vs DCP and vs S-NCP, to Table 8.
3. Compute and report the ESS of the weights within the upper calibration stratum, which is the relevant precision for that column, and apply the >= 50 filter on it.

issues.title: Highlights overstate the evidence: "smallest on 31 datasets" and coverage of "rare, extreme outcomes"
issues.evidence:
Highlight 4, "SDLC gave the smallest stratum-valid sets on 31 datasets, confirmed on 17", reads as SDLC being smallest on every dataset. From results/per_dataset_main_v3.csv (nsize):
- SDLC is smallest among the five primary stratified methods (BCCP, S-NCP, S-CQR, S-HPD, SDLC) on 21/31 datasets, and among the six including SDLC-N on 17/31.
- The ordering depends on the aggregate. The arithmetic mean of normalised size is lower for S-NCP (1.3465) than for SDLC (1.3489), whereas the geometric mean (0.897 vs 0.874) and median favour SDLC.
- Cycle-1 C1-09 flagged this disagreement between summaries. The response says geometric mean and HL are now reported, but the arithmetic-mean reversal is not disclosed.

Highlight 2, "Calibrating within target strata guarantees coverage of rare, extreme outcomes", repeats the wording that C1-03 asked to restrict to calibrated strata. Top-1% coverage is 0.736 for SDLC (Table 2), well below nominal, and the paper itself says the top 1% "is not calibrated".
issues.corrective_action:
1. Highlight 4: "SDLC gave the smallest stratum-valid sets on average (smallest on 21 of 31 datasets); replicated on 17 held-out datasets".
2. Highlight 2: "Calibrating within target strata guarantees coverage within each calibrated target stratum".
3. In Section 6.3 (or in the Table 5 caption), add one sentence: "By the arithmetic mean of normalised sizes, S-NCP (1.347) and SDLC (1.349) are indistinguishable; the geometric mean and median favour SDLC."

issues.title: The "smaller than S-NCP" claims rest on a signed-rank test of strongly skewed log ratios; the promised sign-test column and the requested size TOST are missing
issues.evidence:
Section 5.6 says size comparisons are summarised with the numbers of wins and losses and the sign test. Table 5, Table S5 and Table 7 show only Wilcoxon Holm p; the sign-test p (p_sign in statistics_v3.json) is never printed.

For SDLC vs S-NCP the 95% bootstrap CI of the geometric-mean ratio, the stated primary summary, includes 1 in most analyses:

| Analysis | GM ratio [95% CI] |
|---|---|
| Primary | 0.975 [0.941, 1.020] |
| Excl. development | [0.940, 1.027] |
| Excl. development + diagnostic | [0.930, 1.037] |
| alpha = 0.05 | 0.990 [0.951, 1.047] |
| S3 | [0.922, 1.008] |
| S10 | [0.950, 1.023] |
| Held out (C-H3) | [0.940, 1.028] |
| Held out, S-HPD | [0.963, 1.014] |

The per-dataset log ratios are strongly right-skewed: scipy.stats.skew = 2.79, driven by socmob +0.493 and cars +0.181 (computed from per_dataset_main_v3.csv). Under skewness the signed-rank test can reject because of asymmetry rather than a shift. Its location estimate is the pseudo-median (HL 0.962), not the geometric mean. The sign test (27/4, p = 3.4e-5) supports "smaller on most datasets" robustly, but it is not shown.

The Wilcoxon and sign tests also disagree elsewhere:
- alert rate SDLC vs S-NCP: Wilcoxon p = 0.0175 (Holm 0.035), sign test p = 0.36 (12/18);
- hull vs S-NCP-hull: Wilcoxon Holm p = 0.034 with geometric mean 1.014.

The cycle-1 C1-02 item 4 TOST for size equivalence (margin ±5%) was neither reported nor declined. Computed with tests.tost_wilcoxon on log ratios, margin log(1.05): p = 0.145 on CTR23 and 0.054 held out, so neither a difference in mean nor equivalence is established.

The bootstrap CIs are percentile intervals (tests.bootstrap_ci). Cycle-1 C1-30(b) asked for BCa for geometric-mean ratios, which matters given this skewness.
issues.corrective_action:
1. Add a "Sign p (Holm)" column to Table 5, Table S5 and Table 7, and to the alert-rate statement in Section 6.7. Adjust the sign tests by Holm within the same families.
2. Word every S-NCP/S-HPD size claim as "smaller on most datasets (median/HL ratio X; sign test p)", noting that the geometric-mean CI includes 1, as Section 6.5 already does. Apply this in Section 6.3's first paragraph, the robustness paragraph and Section 6.8.
3. Report the ±5% TOST result for SDLC vs S-NCP (p = 0.145 CTR23; 0.054 held out) in one sentence, or state explicitly that it was not done and why.
4. Switch the geometric-mean CIs to BCa (scipy.stats.bootstrap with method='BCa'), or justify the percentile interval. Re-running analyze3.py takes minutes.

issues.title: Rendering and formatting errors in reported p-values
issues.evidence:
- manuscript_filled.md line 272: "one-sided Holm-adjusted $p\le$ < 0.001", and twice more in the same paragraph.
- Line 310: "TOST with margin 0.01: $p\le$ < 0.001".
- Both render as "p ≤ < 0.001".
- Line 462: "Holm $p$ < 0.001 or smaller" (meaningless).
- Table 7: "median difference -0.0000".
- Table S8 prints "runs_with_inf" (87, 32, 2) also for the marginal methods SCP/NCP/CQR, to which it does not apply.
issues.corrective_action:
1. In render_manuscript.py, emit "$p$ < 0.001" (drop \le) when the formatted value starts with "<". Replace "< 0.001 or smaller" with "< 0.001".
2. Print -0.0000 as 0.000 (or in scientific notation, -1.4e-05).
3. Set runs_with_inf to "–" for marginal methods in Table S8.

issues.title: Some reported p-values are unadjusted although Section 5.6 says families are Holm-corrected; the Holm families are not documented
issues.evidence:
- The alert/cost tests in statistics_v3.json 'alerts' have no p_holm field. Section 6.7 quotes p = 0.130 and p = 0.083 unadjusted, and the low-side cost r=20 SDLC vs TC-LS (p = 0.036) is unreported.
- The Section 6.9 Spearman correlations are unadjusted (6 tests in error_analysis). "weakly related to predictability (rho = 0.38, p = 0.034)" would have Holm p ≈ 0.10.
- The paper never lists the Holm families. For example, "Extreme coverage vs stratified" holds 16 tests (top-5%, top-1%, tilt gamma = 1, 2 × 4 comparators), and SDLC vs SDLC-N is counted in two families ("H3 size (secondary)" and "Decomposition").
- Section 5.2 says the main comparisons are repeated without the ten development and diagnostic datasets, but H1 is repeated only without the three development datasets (n = 28).
issues.corrective_action:
1. Either Holm-adjust the alert comparisons within a family (rule × cost ratio) and the six Spearman correlations, or label them "unadjusted, descriptive" in Sections 6.7 and 6.9. Soften the rho = 0.38 sentence.
2. Add a short supplementary table listing each Holm family: name, members, sidedness, metric.
3. Run H1 also without the dev + diagnostic datasets (one extra call of family() in analyze3.py), or correct Section 5.2.

issues.title: The null reference treats seeds as independent and is applied to floor variants at the wrong level
issues.evidence:
null_worst_stratum (code/scripts/analyze.py lines 107-135) draws an independent Beta-binomial coverage per seed and averages over seeds. The 10 seeds are re-partitions of the same finite dataset, so calibration-conditional coverages are positively correlated across seeds. The null spread of the seed-average is therefore underestimated, and the 5% quantile is too high (anti-conservative for flagging).

This does not threaten the stratified conclusions (1-2 of 31 flagged; 1 of 17 held out), but the method should be described as an approximation.

Table S9 reports "n_ds_below_null" of 28, 23 and 29 for BCCP-floor, S-NCP-floor and SDLC-floor. These variants target 1 - beta = 0.8 in the tail strata but are compared with a 1 - alpha null, which suggests they are invalid.
issues.corrective_action:
1. In Section 5.5, state that the null assumes independent splits and is therefore approximate (conservative for claiming validity).
2. Optionally add a sensitivity null that resamples whole seeds (or uses the empirical seed-to-seed variance of the stratified methods).
3. In Table S9, compute the null for floor variants at their nominal per-stratum level, or show "n/a" with a footnote.
